title: 222 baseline leak leaves are withdrawn to Unknown because the leaked identity is named in a refused statement; 128 of them the reading validated, so the projection can accuse them again only once the refused statement is modelled
why: Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT implemented W44-REFUSED-HANDOFF-LEAK-CLAIMS: a tracked identity the hand-on reader sees named in a refused statement (a store value, a return operand, a call argument, an operand, `&x` or an interior address) carries an unresolved effect, and no leak is claimed through one. Beyond the 30 refused-escape leaves and the cast return, it withdrew 222 baseline leaves in 54 functions (docs/reports/w44-leak-pin-audit/handoff-classification.json). The frozen reading of those 222 is kept: 128 were class (a) validated (118 unit-test failure paths, most of whose buffer is handed to an uncontracted test writer such as ut_build_valid_msgset_v2, ut_write_msgset_v2_header or rd_kafka_buf_new_shadow; 10 library error paths), and 94 were class (c) (44 an uncontracted destructor releases, 37 a call retains, 7 scalar branch correlation, 5 borrowed mk_list_add, 1 undecided null test). The withdrawal is the fail-closed direction (Unsafe -> Unknown, never Safe) but costs the true accusations. Discharge condition: per refused statement, a faithful contract, a validated W4 summary or an admission that models what it does with the identity, so the leaf is re-decided rather than withdrawn, measured by an arbiter that attributes each leaf that returns; W44-CORPUS-CALLEE-SUMMARIES is the likely route for the corpus-defined helpers.

title: mk_list_add is declared borrowed on both positions, so a Monkey object linked into a caller-reachable list is still accused at the next exit (8 leaves)
why: providers/qcore-provider-libevent/contracts/monkey/intrusive_list.qcore declares mk_list_add(entry, head) resource_borrowed on both parameters. Linking `&obj->_head` into a list reachable from the caller publishes `obj`, which a borrowed position does not state, so card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT's audit found 8 class (c) leak leaves in 7 functions whose accusation rests on that silence (mk_rconf_meta_add, mk_rconf_read, mk_rconf_section_entry_add, mk_sched_worker_cb_add, mk_vhost_set_property, mk_vhost_set_single 2, mk_vhost_create 1); reading shows each object linked into its caller's configuration, server or host. Discharge condition: a vocabulary or contract that states an intrusive insertion's publication of the containing object (the v1 `resource_stored` relation over an interior address, or an equivalent), with gateway and Lean parity, and an arbiter attributing each withdrawn leaf. After the refused hand-on rule, 5 of the 8 are also withdrawn (the object is named in a refused statement on the path); 3 stay published (mk_vhost_create, mk_vhost_set_property, mk_vhost_set_single).

title: 7 provisional leak leaves ride a branch combination no execution takes (a flag, a pass counter, a re-validation of the same bytes)
why: The custody projection does not correlate branches on scalar values. Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT's audit found 7 class (c) leaves whose only witness combines branch outcomes no execution combines: decode_histogram_points (cmt_decode_prometheus_remote_write.c) 4, whose witness skips the `static_metric_detected == CMT_FALSE` cleanup arm although the leaked metric exists only on that flag value, and rd_kafka_snappy_java_uncompress (snappy.c) 3, two of whose pass-2 failure arms re-check bytes pass 1 accepted and one of which needs outbuf allocated before its own pass-1 allocation. They stay provisional Unsafe. Discharge condition: a path-sensitivity or relational-scalar refinement with gateway and Lean parity that decides these arms, measured by an arbiter; or a recorded decision that such leaves stay provisional. After the refused hand-on rule all 7 are also withdrawn to Unknown (each identity is named in a refused statement on the path), so no published leak rests on this mechanism now; it decides them again once those statements are modelled.

title: 2 provisional leak leaves sit on the null arm of a null test the projection could not decide
why: Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT found 2 class (c) leaves whose exit is the arm on which the allocation failed, but whose null test the projection did not refine: mk_sched_add_connection (mk_scheduler.c:210, `if (!conn)`, undecided because the other arm's refused cast copy `conn = (struct mk_sched_conn *) data;` poisoned the joined binding) and rd_kafka_snappy_java_uncompress (snappy.c:1712, `unlikely(!outbuf)` inside a refused __builtin_expect call). Discharge condition: a refinement that keeps a null edge's site withdrawal when the test is undecided only through a poisoned join, or admits the __builtin_expect wrapper as the test it wraps, each with Lean parity and a measured arbiter. After the refused hand-on rule, rd_kafka_snappy_java_uncompress's leaf is withdrawn; mk_sched_add_connection's stays published.

title: direct_assignment_destination spells `(*map)->opts = …` as the place `opts`, conflating a caller-reachable member with a local-looking name
why: legacy_c::direct_assignment_destination returns the first suffix of the destination tokens that canonical_place spells, so `(*map)->opts = calloc(...)` binds the acquisition to the place `opts`. Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT found it behind 2 class (c) leak leaves of unpack_basic_type (cmt_decode_msgpack.c:1759 and :1814), where the object is stored into the caller's `*map`. The same reading is a hazard in the discharging direction: a body with a real local `opts` would have the member's identity bound to it, so a release of the local could be credited to the member's acquisition. Discharge condition: refuse (or spell faithfully) a destination whose leading tokens are not a declaration's specifiers, measured by an arbiter, with any verdict movement attributed. The repair belongs to W44-ASSIGNMENT-DESTINATION-SUFFIX-PLACE (registered by W44-INDIRECT-CALL-ARGUMENT-ACCESS, which pins the discharging-direction hole `recs[i].name = x_dup(s); x_free(name);` certifying Safe); this entry records the two corpus leak leaves of unpack_basic_type as its evidence and should be merged into that entry on integration. The refused hand-on rule does not withdraw them: no refused statement names the object.

title: `d = safe = rd_malloc(n)` binds the call's result to `d` only; the inner destination is dropped, not refused
why: Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT found rd_kafka_sasl_safe_string's one leak (rdkafka_sasl_scram.c:249) to rest on the parser binding a chained assignment's call result to its outer destination only: `safe`, which the function returns, stays unbound, so `return safe;` escapes nothing. A dropped write that is neither modelled nor refused is a precision loss in the accusing direction here and, symmetrically, could leave a release through the inner name unmatched. Discharge condition: model or refuse a chained assignment's inner destinations, measured by an arbiter.

title: dlopen/dlclose stay undeclared after the cast-return repair; declaring them needs a library-handle kind
why: RETURN-CAST-PLACE-NOT-ESCAPED's gateway half is discharged by card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT: `return (rd_dl_hnd_t *) handle;` is now decided as `return handle;` (crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/leak_pin_audit.rs). Its second half, re-measuring the dlopen/dlclose declarations W43-DESCRIPTOR-RESOURCE-TRACKING withdrew (5 leaves in 4 functions: mk_plugin_load_dynamic, rd_dl_open0, mk_plugin_load, rd_dl_close; each callee sole-blocking one function), is not done: the declarations need the `dynamic_library` kind that card withdrew with them, a vocabulary addition in providers/quirin-provider-libc. Discharge condition: the kind and the two declarations with loader, gateway and Lean parity, measured by an arbiter that attributes every moved leaf.

title: A non-pointer cast of a returned name the declaration reader does not commit to keeps the place-less exit rather than a refusal
why: Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT's cast-return rule refuses an integer cast of a name the reader commits to as a pointer and any cast of a possible descriptor other than (int), but a non-pointer cast (`(long) h`, `(my_handle_t) h`) of a name whose declared type the reader does not commit to (a pointer typedef, an unreadable declaration) keeps the pre-card place-less exit: never an escape, and the accusing direction if `h` holds an identity, but not the refusal a pointer-to-integer crossing should be. It moved no corpus leaf. Discharge condition: a typedef-resolving pointer test for the operand, or a flow-sensitive refusal that fires when the operand is bound to a tracked identity, with Lean parity and a measured arbiter.

title: The refused hand-on rule reads hand-ons per preprocessed line (condition and statement tables), and its unresolved effect joins by union
why: Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT's rule (legacy_refused_operands.rs) keys what a statement hands on by preprocessed line, because a CFG node carries its line and not its tokens. Each line keeps a condition table (an if/while/switch controlling expression, every for clause) and a statement table; a node refused as a condition reads the first, any other refused node the second, so RD_UT_ASSERT(strlen(p) > 0, ...) does not withdraw p through the refused fprintf beside it. Several statements a macro expands onto one line still union within a table, and the unresolved effect joins by union, so a path to an exit that never passes the refused statement loses its accusation when joined with one that does (QCore.RefusedHandOnCustody.the_union_join_withdraws_a_clean_path). Both approximations only withdraw, never accuse or discharge. Discharge condition: statement-granular hand-on sets carried on the refused node and a path-precise withdrawal, with Lean parity and a measured re-pin; or a recorded decision that the approximation stands.

title: The hand-on reader assumes a member read or write through an identity does not hand the identity on
why: Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT's hand-on reader does not count `p->len`, `p->buf[i]`, `p->fn(...)` or an assignment destination (`p->f = ...`, `*out = ...`, `p[i] = ...`) as naming `p`, so a refused statement that only reads or writes through `p` keeps the accusation about `p` (the first reader, which matched the root name, withdrew mk_net_conn_create's true leak through `mk_net_fd_connect(conn->fd, ...)`). A self-referencing member, such as an empty intrusive list head read as `p->head.next`, yields `p` itself and breaks the assumption in the accusing direction only: the rule withdraws less, never discharges. Discharge condition: a typed reading of member values that recognises a member able to hold the identity or an interior address of it, with Lean parity and a measured arbiter; or a recorded decision that the assumption stands.

title: The refused hand-on rule adds 18 and removes 3 unknown_alias diagnostics on the corpus; the 3 removals in rd_string_render are not localised
why: Card W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT's AFTER arbiter, compared with the rule-off tree, moves unknown_alias by +18 / -3 and nothing else besides the withdrawn leaks. The 18 additions are later uses of an identity the rule marked unresolved, which an Owned or aggregate position reports as an unresolved identity (initialize_metrics_data 1, initialize_resource_metrics 3, the two otlp_*_value_initialize pairs 4, append_metric_to_timeseries 1, flb_input_chunk_write_header_v2 9). The 3 removals are the rd_free(buf) error exits of rd_string_render (rdstring.c:109, :121, :134), inside a loop whose refused `callback(tmpkey, buf + of, ...)` hands buf on; a reduced fixture did not reproduce them, so the mechanism is not localised. No status moves (rd_string_render keeps 21 refusals and stays Unknown), and an unknown_alias is never an accusation or a discharge. Discharge condition: the removal localised to a transfer and either shown to be the fail-closed reading or repaired, with a pinned fixture.
